comparisons.peer_summary: Client net revenue increased to $7.1 billion in 2024 from $4.7 billion in 2023, a 52% increase driven by a 34% rise in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose revenue performance in their Client segments (notebooks/desktops) for 2024, highlighting a recovery in demand. Intel reports Notebook revenue of $19.1 billion, up $2.1 billion from 2023, driven by a 12% increase in volume as customer inventory levels improved, while ASPs remained flat. Similarly, AMD reports Client net revenue increased by 52% to $7.1 billion, driven by a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in ASPs. Both companies attribute revenue growth in this segment to normalization of customer inventory and increased unit shipments compared to the prior year.

sentences.text: ▪CCG revenue increased $1.0 billion from 2023. Notebook revenue was $19.1 billion in 2024, up $2.1 billion from 2023. Notebook volume increased 12% from 2023, as customer inventory levels improved compared to higher levels in 2023. Notebook ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Desktop revenue was $9.7 billion, down $516 million from 2023. Desktop volume decreased 5% from 2023, primarily due to lower demand compared to 2023. Desktop ASPs were roughly flat with 2023. Other CCG revenue was $1.6 billion, down $530 million from 2023, primarily driven by the exit of legacy businesses.

Client net revenue of $7.1 billion in 2024 increased by 52%, compared to net revenue of $4.7 billion in 2023, primarily due to a 34% increase in unit shipments and a 13% increase in average selling price driven by strong demand for AMD mobile and desktop Ryzen processors.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel (in its NEX segment) and AMD (in its Embedded segment) disclose revenue declines in 2024 driven by inventory normalization and lower demand in specific end markets. Intel's NEX revenue increased only $68 million, with 5G customers tempering purchases to reduce existing inventories. AMD's Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion, primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels. Both disclosures explicitly link performance to the industry-wide trend of customers drawing down inventory.
